1. (Currently amended) A proofed frozen dough comprising: (a) gas bubbles dispersed throughout the dough matrix, wherein the gas bubbles comprise carbon dioxide produced by yeast during proofing; (b) a spent yeast component comprising yeast that has been metabolically exhausted during proofing, wherein at least 60 wt.% of the spent yeast component is non-viable; and (c) a preserved yeast component comprising protected yeast that retains at least 50 % of its initial vitality after freezing and storage, wherein the preserved yeast component is capable of producing additional carbon dioxide during baking after thawing.

2. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 1 to about 8 wt.% of the spent yeast component.

3. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component comprises yeast from cream yeast, compressed yeast, semi-dry yeast, frozen yeast, active dry yeast, instant yeast, or a combination thereof.

4. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 3, wherein the yeast has been spent during proofing.

5. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the spent yeast component has a yeast vitality of less than 25 % of its initial vitality.

6. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component has a yeast vitality of at least 50 % of its initial vitality.

7. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough comprises about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the preserved yeast component.

8. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the preserved yeast component comprises encapsulated yeast, fat-coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating protects the yeast from freezing stress and extends shelf life.

9. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a volume, and wherein the gas bubbles make up about 30 to about 90 % of the volume of the frozen dough, and wherein the gas bubbles are produced during a proofing stage prior to freezing.

10. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the proofed frozen dough has a density of about 0.2 to about 0.5 g/cm³.

11. (Currently amended) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the gas bubbles comprise gas produced by the spent yeast component during proofing, and wherein the preserved yeast component produces additional gas during baking.

12. (Original) The proofed frozen dough of claim 1, wherein the frozen dough is in its final shape and form for baking.

13. (Currently amended) A method for making a frozen dough product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough composition, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated and unprotected; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or protected; (b) proofing the dough for a sufficient time to metabolically exhaust at least 60 % of the first yeast and produce carbon dioxide, wherein during proofing the first yeast is spent and the second yeast remains protected and viable; and (c) freezing the dough after proofing, wherein the second yeast retains viability for post-thaw leavening during baking.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 60 % of the first yeast is spent during proofing.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein at least 50 % of the second yeast is preserved during proofing.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast in that the second yeast is encapsulated or protected while the first yeast is unencapsulated and unprotected.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating protects the yeast during freezing and storage.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing comprises mixing the water, flour, and first yeast for a first period of time, adding the second yeast and mixing the dough ingredients for a second period of time, wherein the first period of time is longer than the second period of time, such that the first yeast is substantially spent before the second yeast is added.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 20, wherein the second period of time is from about 1 to about 2 minutes.

22. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising: shaping and cutting the dough to produce a pizza crust prior to proofing; freezing the pizza crust; and applying toppings to the frozen pizza crust.

23. (Original) The method of claim 13, further comprising refrigerating the dough after freezing.

24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the dough is refrigerated for from about 12 hours to about 7 days.

25. (Currently amended) A method for making a leavened bakery product, the method comprising: (a) mixing dough ingredients to produce a dough, the dough ingredients comprising: i. water; ii. flour; iii. a first yeast that is unencapsulated and unprotected; and iv. a second yeast that is encapsulated or protected; (b) proofing the dough to produce a proofed dough, wherein the first yeast is spent during the proofing by producing carbon dioxide and the second yeast is preserved and remains viable during the proofing; (c) freezing the proofed dough, wherein the second yeast retains viability during frozen storage; and (d) thawing and baking the dough to produce the leavened bakery product, wherein the second yeast produces additional carbon dioxide during baking.

26. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast is different from the first yeast in that the second yeast is encapsulated or protected while the first yeast is unencapsulated and unprotected.

27. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the second yeast comprises encapsulated yeast, fat coated yeast, non-hydrated active dry yeast, non-hydrated instant yeast, non-hydrated semi-dry yeast, non-hydrated frozen yeast, or a combination thereof, wherein the encapsulation or coating protects the yeast during freezing and storage.

28. (Original) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough does not comprise chemical leaveners.

29. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough has a first volume before the proofing step, a second volume after the proofing step, and a third volume after the baking step, and wherein the third volume is at least 50 % greater than the second volume due to leavening by the second yeast during baking.

30. (Currently amended) The method of claim 29, wherein the third volume is greater than the second volume due at least in part to an activity of the second yeast during the baking step, wherein the second yeast produces carbon dioxide after thawing.

31. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 20 to about 40 wt.% water and about 50 to about 70 wt.% flour.

32. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 1 to about 7 wt.% of the first yeast.

33. (Currently amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the dough ingredients comprise about 0.1 to about 2 wt.% of the second yeast.
